questions.text: Is the CRC value of the resulting message defined to equal zlib.crc32 of the 4 bytes 'dcba' (0x64,0x63,0x62,0x61)? Answer yes if the requirements fix this without a prior INIT. (Scenario: After reset deasserts, with no CTRL write yet, the host pushes one PUSH4 word 0x61626364 and then reads CRC.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.evidence: - Reset: CRC state is the start value 0xFFFFFFFF internally, so CRC reads 0x00000000 for no bytes (the final XOR is applied on read); BYTE_COUNT 0, BUSY_CYCLES 0, TAIL_LEN 0, CTRL 0.

questions.text: What is BUSY_CYCLES? (REQ-09 only defines N full words; does the tail add a cycle?) (Scenario: After INIT, 5 PUSH4 words are written back-to-back followed by one PUSH_N with TAIL_LEN=2. BUSY_CYCLES is read after the datapath is idle.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: BUSY_CYCLES counts one per clock in which a push is processed, PUSH4 or PUSH_N with N>0. In the scenario, 5 PUSH4 words plus one PUSH_N with TAIL_LEN=2 gives 6, so the tail does add a cycle. A PUSH_N with N=0 would not count.
questions.evidence: BUSY_CYCLES counts one per clock in which a push is processed (PUSH4 or PUSH_N with N>0), it is 32 bits and wraps; a PUSH_N with N = 0 does not count.

questions.text: How many bytes are fed to the CRC and added to BYTE_COUNT? (Scenario: A PUSH_N write is issued with TAIL_LEN field value 4 or greater (e.g. 5), after INIT, wdata=0x11223344.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: TAIL_LEN cannot hold a value of 4 or greater, because only bits 1:0 are stored. Writing 5 stores 1, so PUSH_N pushes 1 byte (the low byte, 0x44) into the CRC and BYTE_COUNT increases by 1.
questions.evidence: TAIL_LEN values above 3 cannot be written: the upper bits are ignored (only bits 1:0 are stored).

questions.text: After both settle, is the previous word included in CRC and BYTE_COUNT (yes) or are all cleared to zero (no)? Answer yes if the word is still reflected. (Scenario: On the same clk cycle the host writes CTRL bit 0 = 1 (INIT) while a previous PUSH4 write from the preceding cycle is still being applied to the CRC datapath.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: no - after both settle, INIT has cleared everything. The previous cycle's push is applied first, then INIT takes effect in the following clock and clears the CRC state, BYTE_COUNT and BUSY_CYCLES. Only a push in the same clock as INIT is dropped.
questions.evidence: INIT written takes effect in the clock after the write and clears CRC state, BYTE_COUNT and BUSY_CYCLES; it wins over a PUSH4 or PUSH_N in the same clock (the push is dropped).

questions.text: What value does h_rdata show for that read? (Scenario: At the same clk edge, h_we writes SCRATCH=0x12345678 and h_re reads SCRATCH, whose previous value was 0xAAAAAAAA.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?

questions.text: Does SCRATCH read 0 and does the CRC register read 0x00000000 (the value that would result from an INIT)? (Scenario: After rst deasserts following power-up, with no CTRL write yet, the host reads SCRATCH (0x008), CRC, BYTE_COUNT and BUSY_CYCLES.) Two careful readers of the requirements disagree about this; what is the intended behaviour?
questions.answer: Yes. After reset SCRATCH reads 0. CRC reads 0x00000000, because the internal state is 0xFFFFFFFF and the final XOR is applied on read. BYTE_COUNT and BUSY_CYCLES both read 0. No INIT write is needed for this. The SCRATCH reset value comes from its register-table row: '32 bits, reads back what was written, resets to 0'.
questions.evidence: - Reset: CRC state is the start value 0xFFFFFFFF internally, so CRC reads 0x00000000 for no bytes (the final XOR is applied on read); BYTE_COUNT 0, BUSY_CYCLES 0, TAIL_LEN 0, CTRL 0.

questions.text: What does BYTE_COUNT read after the push? (Scenario: BYTE_COUNT has reached 0xFFFFFFFC after pushes since INIT and one more PUSH4 is written.) The requirements do not say; what should happen?
questions.answer: BYTE_COUNT wraps modulo 2^32, so after the PUSH4 it reads 0x00000000 (0xFFFFFFFC + 4).
questions.evidence: - BYTE_COUNT is 32 bits and wraps. BUSY_CYCLES counts one per clock in which a push is processed (PUSH4 or PUSH_N with N>0), it is 32 bits and wraps; a PUSH_N with N = 0 does not count.
